analysis: This batch contains only documentation changes: CHANGELOG.md tail context (head lines 3475-4238, historical release notes, unchanged content in this range) and the removal of five changelog.d fragments (cli-download-progress-line, cluster-balanced-equal-cut, cluster-bonsai-residual-and-gate-pressure, cluster-capability-honesty, cluster-cdn-manifest-pins). There are no code, config, protocol or workflow changes in the supplied units, so no direct effect on assets A-001..A-019 or boundaries TB-002/003/007/011/012/013 is visible. The removed fragments are presumably folded into the v0.10.6 candidate section of CHANGELOG.md (head lines 11-808). Only the tail of that section was supplied. I could not verify the folded text against the code. Fragments describe behaviors with security relevance: cluster-capability-honesty (unknown content-part types refused with 400, media capability registration gated on pair mode), cluster-cdn-manifest-pins (model manifest repair writes only when the published manifest names the same model, version, aggregate and files; relevant to A-004/T-012 weight integrity), and cluster-bonsai (memory gate behavior). These are described as already-implemented changes. They were not introduced in this PR's supplied diff, so no regression can be asserted. The new two-Mac cluster feature (RDMA/Thunderbolt peer, cluster_runtime registration block, pair approvals derived from releases) is new attack surface and a trust boundary absent from the canonical threat model; the code implementing it was not supplied here. A later pass that sees the code should check whether the threat model needs a cluster boundary (peer authentication over the cable, E2E plaintext exposure to the second Mac, manifest repair integrity, cluster_runtime attestation and pair approvals). This is a coverage limit, not a finding.
